name: Rack focus, left thread
summary: The phone becomes a three-shot film with the reader as the dolly. SHOT 1 (first screen): the cloche film sits full-bleed behind the hero text at a 1.88x "cover" scale, soft (mip-level blur in the existing WebGL painter, a pre-blurred still as poster/fallback), under a heavy top-weighted scrim; the dome's rainbow rim glows under the ghost link as the only promise of what is under the lid. SHOT 2 (the pin, 25-200vh): as the words leave, the camera racks focus and pulls back (blur to sharp, scale 1.88 to 1, the box sliding from 22lvh to 6lvh) so the whole cloche sits on its plate with the camera locked by the time the lid starts to lift; the lid rises over 65vh of scroll (half the film's own speed) into a top fog, the mark settles and is held on frame 232 (7.733 s), never past it. SHOT 3 (birth): a bright glint wakes on the ribbon's left extreme, a short S-curl peels off the left lobe and dives into a rail 10px from the left edge at 58lvh; at 200vh the sticky frame lets go and the page line continues from that exact point, its head pinned to the 58lvh reading line, wandering 4px either side of the rail like a slow snake past every beat (crests toward headlines, troughs at props), crossing the full-bleed cloud stills, until it turns into the storymark's left lobe at the resolve, draws the figure-eight in its own rail colours, thickens into the ribbon under #infg, and dissolves into the real mark while the wordmark fades in and its rule draws from the left, the desktop's own gesture. Every rule lives under html.story.pfilm and every JS branch under phoneOn, so the desktop executes today's statements byte for byte; reduced motion never gets pfilm and keeps today's static story. WHAT I WOULD NOT DO: (1) CSS filter:blur() on the live canvas (a 3-5 Mpx Gaussian per scroll frame on iOS; the mip blur is one draw and the still cross-fade is free); (2) scrub a <video> element on the phone (100-300 ms seeks on iOS read as a broken video; the no-decoder path is a three-still dissolve instead); (3) position:fixed for the frame (the iOS URL bar resizes it and clears the WebGL backbuffer; sticky inside a 300lvh box is constant); (4) mask-image on the film box (an offscreen layer pass at dpr 3; two gradient fog strips do the same dissolve for nothing); (5) use the film's 8.0-9.6 s up-right unravel or the 233-239 "end lets go" frames (the line leaves LEFT, from the left lobe, so the ribbon must stay closed while it is born); (6) pin the resolve lockup (a second sticky region inside the flex stage fights the contact bar; scrubbing the merge by the mark's own screen position is what the desktop does anyway); (7) 100dvh anywhere, scroll-snap, scroll-driven CSS animations, SVG filters, backdrop-filter over the film; (8) a single 16:9 encode at cover scale (four fifths of the picture off screen and the mark 500px wide at the reveal): the phone gets its own 936x1080 crop of the cloche.

heroLayout: FIRST SCREEN (390x844 lvh; all vertical sizes in lvh so the iOS URL bar never re-lays it out; the text row uses svh only for its min-height). Header .hdr fixed 52px, transparent at scrollY 0; under html.story.pfilm .hdr.is-scrolled gets background rgba(10,10,10,.96) and NO backdrop-filter (the filter over a WebGL layer re-composites the canvas every frame on iOS). .stage keeps its padding-top (hdr + 10lvh = 136px at 390). .band--hero .band__in stays in flow at z-index 2 over the film: h1 .hl--hero at --hero-size 11.3vw = 44px, 'WE'LL POST THE SPECIALS.' two lines with SPECIALS. in acc italic, 'YOU KEEP COOKING THEM.' at .7em in ink-3, block 136-279px; sub 17px two lines 305-358 with its 56px indent; .btn--primary full width 388-440; .btn--ghost 450-494 wrapped (white-space normal, underline via text-decoration, the 50%+13px hairline background dropped, per the layout audit) so the arrow is never clipped at 360-390px. Text block bottom at 59lvh, above the 664px small viewport of an iPhone with both bars showing. Below it, 41lvh of film: the blurred dome's top from 58lvh and the plate's rainbow rim at 88-97lvh, the scroll cue. Two GET YOUR PLAN calls stay on the first screen (nav link + button) as today; the nav link is not hidden under pfilm because during the 105vh of pure film it is the only CTA. THE HERO BOX: #hero becomes display:block; position:absolute; top:0; left:0; width:100%; height:var(--pin-box, 300lvh); z-index:0; pointer-events:none; background:#0A0A0A (the page ground, not --film-bg, so the frame dissolves into the page) inside .stage (position:relative, overflow visible; main, .film and .stage must never get overflow other than visible or sticky dies). .band--hero{min-height:calc(var(--pin-box) - var(--stage-pt)); position:relative; z-index:2} so the next band starts at page y 300lvh exactly and the frame is stuck for 200lvh. .hero__frame: position:sticky; top:0; height:100vh; height:100lvh; overflow:hidden; background:#0A0A0A; contains, bottom to top: .hero__box (the film box: poster still, canvas or 2D canvas, the blurred still; transform-only), the top fog <i>, the bottom fog <i>, the scrim ::after, and #snkc (the curl svg, 100% x 100%). Fogs: top = linear-gradient(180deg,#0A0A0A 0 52px,rgba(10,10,10,.85) 60px,rgba(10,10,10,0) 16lvh) as a 0-16lvh strip; bottom = linear-gradient(180deg,rgba(10,10,10,0) 54lvh,rgba(10,10,10,.85) 66lvh,#0A0A0A 78lvh) as a 54-100lvh strip. Scrim ::after = linear-gradient(180deg,rgba(10,10,10,.92) 0,rgba(10,10,10,.90) 60lvh,rgba(10,10,10,.60) 74lvh,rgba(10,10,10,.34) 100%) at opacity var(--hs,1). All three are gradient layers, no filters, no masks. .hero__pulses, .hero__ring, .act--still: display:none under pfilm (the still's <picture> gets a second <source media='(hover:none) and (pointer:coarse) and (max-width:1024px)' srcset=gif> so its 48KB never downloads on the phone). The page's tick ::before on every non-hero band is hidden under pfilm (the snake carries that meaning); .band padding becomes clamp(40px,7vh,64px). Nothing in this block is reachable from html.film.
filmPlacement: ASSET. A phone encode from cloche3d/out: crop=936:1080:864:0 (x 864-1800 of the 1920 frame, aspect .8667) so the closed cloche (x 1020-1710), the lifted lid at 2.7 s (x 930-1800, the reason the crop is 936 and not the 4:5 864: the lid's right edge would be cut by 72px during the lift) and the held mark (x 960-1620, y 380-780) all sit inside; scale=720:832 (0.60 Mpx), frames 0-232 (-frames:v 233; frame 232 = 7.733 s is the last frame with the loop closed at both ends; 233-239 open the bottom-right end and 240+ lean into the up-right unravel, neither is ever shown), same recipe as encode.sh (x264 high 4.0, keyint 8, keyint_min 8, sc_threshold 0, bf 0, bt709 tv, timescale 15360, faststart), crf 25, expected about 0.95-1.05 MB; deliver/hero-scrub-m.mp4. Poster deliver/hero-still-m.jpg = f0000 same crop at 432x498, gblur sigma 7, q 5 (about 18 KB). Stills-path extras (fetched only when there is no decoder): hero-f0-m.jpg (f0000 sharp, 720x832, q 82) and hero-mark-m.jpg (f0232, 720x832, q 82), about 70 KB each. In crop coordinates the mark spans x 10-81%, y 35.2-72.2%, centre (45.5%, 53.7%); the closed cloche x 17-90%, y 36-83%; the plate rim about y 75%. THE BOX. --bw = min(100vw, calc(92lvh * .8667)) (390px on a phone; 311px on an 844x390 landscape phone so it is never taller than the screen; 768px on a portrait tablet), height calc(var(--bw) * 1080 / 936) (450px at 390). Rest placement (the locked camera, u >= 95): left calc(50% - var(--bw)/2) = 0, top 6lvh (51px), transform-origin 50% 0. The mark then sits at x 40-315px, y 209-376px, centre M = (177, 292) = (45vw, 34.6lvh), whole with 40px and 75px side margins, clear of the header (52px) and above the thumb; the plate rim at about 52lvh, the box bottom at 59lvh under the bottom fog. Scroll-driven transform: transform: translateY(var(--hy)) scale(var(--hz)); --hz = S0 - (S0 - 1) * smooth(u,25,95) with S0 = max(100lvh / boxH, 100vw / bw) = 1.876 at 390x844 (1.876 at 430x932 and 360x780 too, 1.16 on a 768x1024 tablet, 1.0 landscape); --hy = 16lvh * (1 - smooth(u,25,95)) so the box top starts at 22lvh (186px) and the cover box (733x844) puts the dome's top at 58lvh and the rim at 88-97lvh under the text on the first screen, then slides up to 6lvh while shrinking to 1.0, a rack focus plus pull-back that lands the whole cloche centred by the time the lid moves. Both are custom properties on .hero__box written by pDraw() through setVar (steps .002 and .1px), compositor-only. The canvas store never follows the box: heroFilm.width/height stay at the encode's 720x832 (the phone branch of sizeFilmCanvas sets viewport 720x832, ts 1/720,1/832, bc 0 so the Catmull-Rom path is off) and the compositor scales; at dpr 3 the 720 store is shown at 1.62x while it is blurred anyway and at 1.62x at the sharp hold, where the glowing tube and the chrome show no softness. The poster still and the stills-path images share the box (position absolute inset 0, width/height 100%, object-fit fill; the aspect is the encode's so nothing is cropped). FILM CLOCK. phoneT = track(PT, u), PT = [[0,0],[30,0],[95,2.7],[160,4.2],[180,5.8],[200,7.733],[1e9,7.733]]: hold on frame 0 while the words are read; steam over 65vh; the lid over 65vh (45 frames, 12px of scroll per frame, half the film's rate, the reveal you can watch); the settle over 20vh; the held mark's shimmer over 20vh; then frame 232 for ever. filmFrame(phoneT) on the WebCodecs path (the existing wantFrame/filmDir/pumpDecoder logic, keepGops 4 = 32 frames = 22 MB at 720x832). Fallback placement is identical for the stills path (the same box, same transform, hero-f0-m.jpg cross-dissolving to hero-mark-m.jpg over u 110-165, the lid-lift window, with opacity only).
blurMethod: PRIMARY (WebGL2 + WebCodecs): a rack focus inside the painter, one draw, no extra layer. When phoneOn and the context is webgl2, makePainter compiles a phone-only program (the desktop's shader source string is untouched): '#version 300 es' fragment with uniform float u_lod; colour = textureLod(u_tex, uv, u_lod) (or texture(u_tex, uv, u_lod) as bias). The texture gets TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR and, after every texImage2D(frame) while u_lod > 0, gl.generateMipmap(TEXTURE_2D) (WebGL2 mipmaps NPOT; 720x832 is 0.6 Mpx, about .4-.8 ms on a mid Adreno/Mali; the call stops once the blur is 0). u_lod = 3.2 * blurAmt, blurAmt = 1 - smooth(u,35,90): LOD 3.2 samples a 90x104-pixel level, equivalent to a 10-12px Gaussian at 390 wide, 'a bit blurred', boxy in the way a soft lens is, not frosted glass; trilinear interpolation between levels makes the focus pull continuous. The uniform is written once per rAF only when it changes by .02. The blurred still (hero-still-m.jpg, gblur 7 at 432px) sits UNDER the canvas as the poster from first paint; on the primary path its job ends when video-ready fires (the canvas fades in over .6 s with the same LOD 3.2 picture, so the hand-over is invisible). FALLBACKS, same numbers: (a) WebGL1 (no NPOT mipmaps) or the 2D-context path (iOS 16.4-16.x, VideoFrame not accepted by texImage2D): the blurred still is moved ABOVE the canvas (.hero__blur, opacity var(--hb) = blurAmt) and cross-fades to the sharp film; because the film is on frame 0 until u=30 and the still is frame 0, the dissolve starts as a perfect match and the steam appears through it. (b) Stills path (no decoder): the blurred still over hero-f0-m.jpg, same --hb. (c) A local toggle for Karan: ?pfilm=cssblur applies filter:blur(calc(10px * var(--hb))) to .hero__box under a .is-blur class removed when --hb reaches 0, so he can compare on his phone; it is not the default because a 733x844 layer at dpr 3 is 5.6 Mpx blurred on every changed frame (2-6 ms, iOS re-rasterises). Legibility is the scrim's job, not the blur's: the gradient scrim at .92 over the words is what takes the worst backdrop from #907456 (ink 3.6:1) to #1F1A16 (ink 14:1, ink-2 5.1:1, acc 5.6:1) on the real frames; the blur just removes edges so the type has nothing to fight. Never backdrop-filter, never mask-image, never an SVG filter on the phone.
lineBirth: WHERE. The film's own unravel leaves top-right from the ribbon's bottom-right end; Karan wants the line to leave LEFT, so it is born from the ribbon's LEFT EXTREME, the point of the left lobe nearest the rail, where the tube's centreline runs vertically. In the locked camera on 390x844 the mark spans x 40-315, y 209-376 (frame px) and the tube is about .13 of the mark's width thick, so the centreline's left extreme is E0 = (40 + .065*275, 292) = (58, 292); in general E0 = (boxLeft + .10*bw + .065*.71*bw, boxTop + .537*boxH) = (boxLeft + .146*bw, boxTop + .537*boxH), published as __pfilm.markRect()/birth(). The film holds frame 232, so the ribbon stays closed under the birth: the line is a thread peeling off the ribbon's outer edge, not the ribbon coming undone. WHEN. u 165-175: the tip (the 72px radial <i>, 2.2px #FFF8EC core, halo to 36px) fades in at E0 to opacity .6 with a slow breath (scale 1 + .25*sin(now*.004)), a glint on the ribbon's edge, while the film plays its held shimmer (t 6.2-7.0 s). u 172-198: the curl draws. u 198-200: the curl is complete, the tip rests at R0f, the frame is about to let go. THE CURL PATH (frame px, inside #snkc, a 100%x100% svg in .hero__frame so it stays with the pinned mark and then scrolls away with the frame): with xr = --rail = gut/2 = 10px, R0f = (xr, K*LVH) with K = .58 (489px), dx = E0.x - xr = 48, dy = R0f.y - E0.y = 197: d = M E0 C (E0.x, E0.y+.15dy) (E0.x+.25dx, E0.y+.26dy) (E0.x-.04dx, E0.y+.41dy) C (E0.x-.33dx, E0.y+.55dy) (xr, E0.y+.61dy) R0f = 'M58 292 C58 322 70 343 56 373 C42 400 10 412 10 489'. It leaves the lobe straight down (tangent continuous with the ribbon), bows 12px outward (the snake's first bend), crosses the gutter, and arrives at the rail exactly vertical (the last control point sits directly above R0f) so the page line continues it without a visible seam (round caps overlap). Lc = getTotalLength(), about 230px; stroke-dasharray Lc, dashoffset Lc*(1 - shownCurl). Draw law: birth = 1 - (1 - smooth(u,172,198))^2 (ease-out: it leaves the mark fast and settles into the rail), shownCurl lerps toward birth in time (see the drawing law), tip at atL(curlMap, shownCurl*Lc) converted to page px (frame y + scrollY while stuck). Threads on the curl: the same four <use>s as the page line (case 5px #000 at .35 over the film, glow 10px url(#snkglitc) .16, body 2.2px url(#snkgc), core .8px #FFF6E8 .5) with the vertical repeating spectrum gradients phase-locked to the page line's (y1c = y1 + fy0 - frameRestTop) so the colour at R0f is the same in both svgs. Colour at birth: CYAN. In the film the left lobe is cyan-blue, the crossing magenta, the right lobe orange (visible on the 5.8-8.0 s frames), so the gradient's phase is chosen so that E0 shows stop .55 (#0FA3C2) and the line runs cyan, blue, purple, magenta, red, orange down the page to arrive yellow at the storymark. THE SEAM. The page line's first point is R0 = (xr, frameRestTop + K*LVH) page px with frameRestTop = heroTop + 200 LVH (the frame's page top once un-stuck); its head follows tipY = scrollY + K*LVH; at the un-stick instant scrollY = frameRestTop so tipY = R0.y: the page line starts to draw at the same scroll, from the same point, at which the curl's end starts to move up with the frame. Before that, target length 0.
linePath: SPACE. #snk is a page-space svg appended to section.film after .stage (position absolute; left 0; top 0; width/height set as attributes in px = film.clientWidth x film.offsetHeight; viewBox 0 0 W H; z-index 3 inside main's stacking context, above the bands' z 2 and below the contact bar's 80 and header's 90; pointer-events none; no transform, no will-change, no filter, ever, so a 390x8000px element is never promoted; Chrome rasterises only the changed tiles when --off moves). Rebuilt by buildSnake() on enable, on document.fonts.ready, on the storymark's load, and from a debounced ResizeObserver on .stage and .act--mark; all measurements use offsetTop chains for the .act props (they carry translateY(18px) until .in, which rects would include) and getBoundingClientRect for the bands. THE RAIL. x = --rail = gut/2 = 10px on a phone (the body 2.2px, the glow 5-15px, the text at 20px; on a tablet with a wider gutter the rail stays at gut/2). Amplitude A = min(4, gut*.2) = 4px. KEYPOINTS, y strictly increasing: R0 = (10, frameRestTop + .58 LVH); a CREST (14, y) at the top of every .band__in of a non-hero band (the line leans toward each headline); a TROUGH (6, y) at the layout top of every prop except .act--still, .act--mark, .act--word (the sky stills, the four .pan cards, the two pair plates); where two consecutive points are more than .6 LVH apart, floor(gap/.6 LVH) intermediate points alternating 14/6 so the line wanders on its own through the long cards; then (10, S0.y - .25 LVH) and S0 = (10, E.y - 1.0 h) to damp the last wave onto the rail. Cubics by Catmull-Rom (c1 = Pi + (Pi+1 - Pi-1)/6, c2 = Pi+1 - (Pi+2 - Pi)/6, ghost points at the ends), which keeps the path monotone in y because every x stays within 10 +- 4 and every y increases. THE ENTRY. The storymark under pfilm is width min(62vw, 280px) centred (242x133 at 390, left edge 74); its ribbon (mark-720.webp: centreline left extreme at .090w, .50h; ribbon thickness .178w) gives E = (Rl + .090w, Rt + .50h) = (96, markCentreY), tangent straight down. The rail's last segment: C (10, E.y - .5h) (E.x, E.y - .6h) E, an S from the gutter into the lobe, vertical in, vertical out. Ls = getTotalLength() (about 6-7k px). lineDrawingLaw: The desktop's law, turned vertical: dasharray on the <g>, inherited by the four <use>s, dashoffset driven by a sampled map and a time lerp toward a scroll target, so the drawn end never jumps and rewinds when the reader scrolls back. MAPS. After a rebuild: sample(snkPath, max(300, Ls/8)) gives xs, ys, ls arrays and L (getPointAtLength runs only here, never per frame); atY(map, y) binary-searches the monotone ys and returns arc length l at page y; atL(map, l) returns the point at arc length l from the samples; the curl (80 samples) and loop (120 samples) have their own maps. TARGETS (pure functions of scrollY, computed per rAF; u = (scrollY - heroTop)/LVH*100 in vh): tipY = scrollY + .58 LVH - fy0 (the reading line; .58 puts the drawn end just below the headline being read and above the thumb); curl target birth(u) = 1 - (1 - smooth(u,172,198))^2; rail target = tipY <= R0.y ? 0 : atY(lineMap, min(tipY, E.y)); loop target = clamp((.58 LVH - markScreenY)/(.18 LVH), 0, 1) where markScreenY = markCentrePageY - scrollY (equivalently (tipY - E.y)/(.18 LVH)); merge rb = smooth(markScreenY, .40 LVH, .30 LVH). LERP. shown += (target - shown) * (1 - .8^(dt/16.667)), dt clamped to 100 ms, snapped to the target within .25px (rail) / .002 (fractions), the same constant the desktop's tick() uses at .16 tuned up to .2 so a phone flick catches up within about 250 ms. WRITES. setVar(curlG,'--off', Lc*(1-shownCurl), .5); setVar(lineG,'--off', Ls - shownL, .5); setVar(loopG,'--off', Ll*(1-shownLoop), .5); --lw, --la, --lb, --rb at .01; the tip's translate3d/opacity via setProp; each write skipped when under its step, so a settled frame writes nothing. Everything happens in ONE requestAnimationFrame kicked by a passive scroll listener (pKick: if pRaf === null and the hero/snake is on screen, schedule); the loop keeps itself alive only while any shown differs from its target or while the tip breathes at the mark (u 165-200), then goes idle. No layout reads on the scroll path: heroTop, LVH (= heroFrame.offsetHeight), fy0, R0, E, the maps and the storymark rect are cached by buildSnake/phoneMeasure and refreshed only by the debounced resize (140 ms, ignoring height-only changes under 25% so the iOS toolbar collapse costs nothing) and the ResizeObserver. On a rebuild the shown values are re-derived from the new map at the same tipY (no lerp across a geometry change). MONOTONE: because the rail is monotone in y and the target is a single-valued function of tipY that clamps at 0 and at atY(E.y), a fast flick draws forward through every point and a scroll-up rewinds the same way; rubber-band (scrollY < 0) is clamped to u = 0 before anything is computed. TIP POSITION: u < 165 none; 165-172 at E0 (page px = frame px + scrollY - fy0); on the curl at atL(curlMap, shownCurl*Lc) while the frame is stuck; on the rail at atL(lineMap, shownL) once shownL > 0; on the loop at atL(loopMap, shownLoop*Ll); opacity .9*(1-lb) after the loop closes. Pulse at beats: for the nearest headline top within +-8vh of tipY, k = 1 - |d|/8vh: tip scale 1 + .3k and body stroke-width 2.2 + .8k px (one custom property --pw on the line group, step .05).

SEQUENCE, all scrubbed by the mark's own screen position (markScreenY = centre y on screen, decreasing as the reader scrolls; equivalent to the reading line with K = .58): (1) ARRIVAL. The rail's last wave damps, the entry cubic turns right into E = the storymark's left extreme (96px, markCentreY) while the mark is still invisible (--rb 0): the reader sees the thread turn in toward an empty space under the headline. (2) THE LOOP (markScreenY 58 to 40 lvh, 18vh of scroll): #snkLoop draws one full circuit from E in the rail's own colours (lbody url(#snkg), 2.2px) with the tip on its drawn end: the left lobe's lower half, the crossing, the right lobe, back through the crossing, the left lobe's upper half, closing at E. The reader watches the line write the mark. At 70% of the circuit the wordmark starts: --rw = smooth(shownLoop,.7,1)*(1) fading DOMIN8TE MEDIA in below (this is what the desktop's wordAct does at p .958-.978, arriving with the loop). (3) THE RIBBON (markScreenY 40 to 30 lvh, rb 0 to 1): la = smooth(rb,0,.55): --lw goes 2.2px to .178w (43px at 390, the ribbon's thickness in mark-720.webp), lbody (rail colours) fades to 0 as lring (url(#infg), the mark's own diagonal sweep, objectBoundingBox so it matches the real ribbon's colour layout exactly as the desktop's #loop does) fades to 1: the thread swells into the ribbon and takes the mark's colours; the join is seamless because the rail arrives showing stop .27 (yellow), which is #infg's colour at the left extreme. lb = smooth(rb,.45,1): the ring's opacity goes to 0 as --rb (the real .act--mark image) goes to 1: the drawn ribbon becomes the photograph of the mark, its glow and depth appearing under the stroke. Scrolling back reverses every step (the mark un-photographs into a ring, thins into a thread, unwrites itself, and the thread retreats up the rail). gating: CLASS. html.story.pfilm, decided in the head gate script (index.tpl.html, beside window.__GATES) BEFORE first paint so the 300lvh hero box, the band's min-height and the sticky frame exist in the first layout (no jump from scroll restoration or scroll anchoring, LCP measured on the real layout): window.__PHONE = '(hover: none) and (pointer: coarse) and (max-width: 1024px)'; in the same IIFE: if (story && !matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches && matchMedia(window.__PHONE).matches) r.classList.add('pfilm'); the no-script check() also removes it. WHY THESE TERMS: hover:none + pointer:coarse describe the primary input, so a desktop window merely narrowed keeps today's static story (Karan compares the desktop by resizing; a mouse wheel has no momentum, no URL bar), Samsung DeX and a touch laptop with a mouse stay desktop, and Chrome/CDP touch emulation (c.size(w,h,true,dpr)) qualifies, which the probes need; max-width:1024px keeps portrait tablets on the phone build and excludes nothing story admits; no orientation term (coarse landscape is already story only via the gate's max-height:560px, and an Android soft keyboard turning 360x640 into 360x340 would otherwise flip the mode while typing in the contact form); prefers-reduced-motion:no-preference is hard constraint 2 and reacts live because the reduce query is already in __GATES and routes through applyMode(). site.js: MQ_PHONE = matchMedia(window.__PHONE), change listener -> applyMode(); phoneWants() = root.classList.contains('story') && !reduced() && MQ_PHONE.matches; applyMode(): if story { disableFilm(); phoneWants() ? enablePhoneFilm() : disablePhoneFilm() } else { disablePhoneFilm(); enableFilm() }; root.classList.toggle('pfilm', phoneOn). Deferred while document.activeElement is an input/textarea/select. PATH CHOICE inside pfilm (layout identical either way): FILM path when 'VideoDecoder' in window && (isConfigSupported for avc1.640028 with hardwareAcceleration 'prefer-software' then 'no-preference', first supported) && a WebGL context is obtainable && !(navigator.connection && (connection.saveData || /(^|-)2g$/.test(connection.effectiveType || ''))) && !matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-data: reduce)').matches; else STILLS path (three JPEGs, same choreography, no MP4 fetch, no <video>). The <video> element is never used for scrubbing on the phone. The line and the merge run on both paths (they do not need the film). Decoder error mid-visit: re-init once from the bytes still held; a second failure switches to the stills path in place (the poster is under the canvas so nothing goes black). TEARDOWN on any gate flip (disablePhoneFilm): remove the scroll listener, IO and RO, cancel the rAF, close the decoder and frames, revoke the blob, clear --hy/--hz/--hs/--hb/--pw/--off/--lw/--la/--lb/--rb/--rw/--rr and the tip's inline styles, remove is-blur/off/pfilm, and if the phone asset was loaded drop it (initHero(url) keyed on heroSrc) so a tablet rotating into film mode loads the desktop file. DESKTOP GUARD: (pointer: fine) never matches __PHONE, so html.film never carries pfilm, phoneOn is always false, and every shared function (sizeFilmCanvas, blit, makePainter, initHero, applyMode, resize, visibilitychange, onPageScroll) takes its old branch; proven by pixel-diffing 1440x900 and 1920x1080 stills at three __feel.at() moments and friction-check.js before/after. TOGGLES for Karan (per his habit): ?pfilm=off (today's story), ?pfilm=still (force the stills path), ?pfilm=film, ?pfilm=cssblur (CSS blur instead of the mip blur), ?pfilm=dbg (a corner readout of __pfilm.state(): path, wc/twoD, groups, slowMs, store, u, t, frame). Debug surface window.__pfilm read-only like __feel.
performance: BUDGET per scroll frame on a mid phone (target < 8 ms on the CDP 4x-throttled probe, < 12 ms worst): one passive scroll listener that stores scrollY and kicks one rAF; in the rAF: track(PT,u) and filmFrame(phoneT) (texture upload of one 720x832 I420 VideoFrame + one quad, about 1-2 ms; generateMipmap only while blur > 0, about .5 ms, gone after u=90); up to 3 setVar writes on .hero__box (--hy, --hz) and the scrim (--hs), all compositor-only (transform/opacity), no layout, no paint; 1 uniform (u_lod) while blurring; 3 dashoffset custom properties (.5px step) and up to 4 more on the loop group; the tip's translate3d. No getBoundingClientRect on the scroll path. The page-tall #snk is never promoted (no transform/will-change/filter), so a dashoffset change re-rasterises only the tiles near the head. The 2D fallback costs 2-5 ms per drawImage(VideoFrame) at 720x832, acceptable at 8-frame GOPs. Decoder: WebCodecs with the existing GOP pump, keepGops 4 = 32 frames = 22 MB at 720x832 (versus 100 MB with the 1080p file), VideoFrames closed as today; on Android with MediaCodec (no software H.264) 'prefer-software' is refused and no-preference is taken; on VideoToolbox the per-GOP flush is 20-60 ms, inside the existing 90 ms slow check, which if tripped (log FD.slowMs) now lands on the stills path, not the video element. Memory lifecycle: hero.off + dropFrames() once the frame has scrolled off (u > 300), refilled by pDraw() on the way back; visibilitychange hidden drops frames, visible calls pDraw(); pagehide closes the decoder, pageshow (bfcache) re-inits from the held bytes; webglcontextrestored re-runs makePainter (phone program) + the phone branch of sizeFilmCanvas which repaints and re-pumps. Network: 0.95-1.05 MB MP4 fetched after the load event with fetch(url,{priority:'low'}), whole-file read (every seek local; no Range dance with the Hostinger CDN), 20 s per-chunk watchdog whose abort lands on the stills path; poster 18 KB with fetchpriority high as the LCP candidate under the text; the desktop's 48 KB still and hero-data.json are never fetched on the phone; the pulses canvas never starts (startPulses is guarded by filmOn). Store sizing: the canvas stays at the encode's 720x832 (never resized on scroll or toolbar collapse, so the WebGL backbuffer is never cleared mid-scroll); the resize handler ignores height-only changes under 25%; orientation change re-measures once after two rAFs. Viewport units: lvh for the frame and the pin (constant while the URL bar moves), svh only for the first screen's min-height, never dvh. Layers on screen during the pin: the canvas (or still), the blurred still (opacity 0 when not needed), two fog gradients, one scrim gradient, the curl svg, the header: six small compositor layers, no filters, no masks, no blend modes, no backdrop-filter (the header's is turned off under pfilm). Scroll behaviour untouched: no touch listeners, no preventDefault, no scroll-snap; during a programmatic smooth jump (the header anchors) the pump paints nearest-decoded frames only until scrollend / 120 ms quiet. Probe: gauntlet/pfilm-check.js with cdp.js at 390x844 touch dpr 2 and 3, 360x780, 430x932, 844x390, 768x1024: assert html.pfilm, getComputedStyle(heroFrame).position === 'sticky' and its rect.top === 0 through u 0-200, __pfilm.frame() within 2 of 0/35/81/126/174/232 at u 0/60/95/160/180/200, --hz 1.876 to 1, no horizontal overflow, no console errors, a scripted 8000px scroll at 60 steps with rAF deltas under 12 ms at 4x CPU throttle; shots pf-<u>.png; plus the desktop parity run and the reduced-motion run diffed against gauntlet/shots/mobile-before/sheet-a/b.png (expect zero diff except the two story-wide legibility fixes, which Karan has to approve).
risks: iOS cannot be driven from this Windows machine: sticky inside the absolute hero box, texImage2D(VideoFrame) on WebGL2 (17+ yes, 16.4-16.x maybe not, then the 2D path), VideoToolbox GOP timing against the 90 ms slow check, and jetsam at 22 MB of frames all need one real iPhone run of ?bare=1&pfilm=dbg; the design degrades to the stills path on every one of those failures rather than to black, but the degrade has to be seen once.

The mip-level blur needs WebGL2 and a phone-only shader program: if the second program is compiled from a branch inside makePainter, a slip there could touch the desktop; keep the desktop shader string literal untouched and select the phone source only when phoneOn, and pixel-diff the desktop before and after.

The 936-wide crop is chosen from the reader's measurement that the lifted lid reaches x 1800 at 2.7 s; if the lid swings wider at 3.0-3.6 s (not on the contact sheet) a strip of chrome could still clip at the crop's right edge during the lift. Check frames f0090-f0110 before encoding; widen to crop=1000:1080:800:0 (720x778) if it does.

The rainbow rim at the plate is the first screen's promise, and it sits at 88-97lvh under the ghost link; on an iPhone with both bars showing (664px small viewport) only the dome's top peeks below the text until the bars collapse on the first scroll. Acceptable, but if Karan wants the rim visible at rest the box's start top drops from 22lvh to 16lvh and the scrim's lower stops lighten.

Position:sticky dies under any ancestor with overflow other than visible/clip: html/body's overflow-x:clip is safe, but a future rule putting overflow:hidden on main, .film or .stage (for instance to contain the line) would silently unpin the film. The line is contained by its coordinates instead; guard with a probe assertion on heroFrame's rect.top.

The loop is drawn in the storymark's rect measured after layout; a late font swap, the resolve headline reflowing, or the mark image loading after the head arrives would put the loop 18px off. Mitigated by eager loading the storymark, rebuilding on fonts.ready/img load/ResizeObserver, and re-deriving shown from the new map; still worth a shot at the resolve after a cold load on a slow connection.

The two story-wide legibility fixes (ghost link wrap, climb ln--2 at .78em, the 4/5 sky figure) change the reduced-motion phone as well, which strictly breaks 'reduced motion keeps today's static story'; they are defects, not taste, but Karan must say yes or they move under pfilm.

Colour continuity at the merge assumes #infg shows yellow at the storymark's left extreme (its 4%,0 to 96%,100% diagonal puts that point near .27) and that mark-720.webp's ribbon follows the same sweep; if the webp's left lobe is not yellow-orange the ring-to-image cross-fade will show a hue jump. Read the webp's pixel at (.09w,.5h) once and set the rail's arrival stop from it instead of the constant .27.

Samsung Internet 21 and older (no WebCodecs) and iOS 15-16.3 land on the stills path: a dissolve from a closed cloche to the held mark instead of the lift. It keeps the story and the line, but Karan should know a slice of Android readers will see a dissolve, not a lift.

Rubber-band at the top on iOS pushes scrollY negative and fires a burst on snap-back; u is clamped at 0 and the frame's background matches the ground, but the film must not be asked for a negative time or flip filmDir during the burst (ignore direction changes while scrollY < 0).
